summary: Alubomulle Sumanasara works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University from circa 1980 to 1985 under Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë works in philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1986–1988) and Harvard University (~1988–1995), later holding posts at CUNY (~1995–1996), UC Santa Cruz (~1996–2003), and UC Berkeley (~2003).

Alvappillai Veluppillai specialized in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Ceylon under K. Kanapathypillai and at Oxford under Thomas Burrow, holding posts at Ceylon, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University.

Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1937–1938). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and was a fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1968–1971).
Amalia Pezzali is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed doctoral studies under T. R. V. Murti and also studied under Michel Hulin.

Amanda K. Goodman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Nath Pandeya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

Amar Singh works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied under Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963) and completed doctoral studies under Anthony Kennedy Warder, also studying with Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and others.
Amara Ali works in linguistics and Indology. She is attested in 2026 as a lecturer in Urdu at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College, where he became Professor of English in 1917. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1947) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).
Amarasvar Thakur was an Indologist who served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series and held a post at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1936.

Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist educated at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1953–1959). He held appointments at Jadavpur, Delhi, the London School of Economics (~1971–1982), and Harvard University (~2004).
Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Hyderabad by 2009 and served there as a professor (attested 2018–2026).

Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated by teachers including M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte, she has held posts at the University of York, University of St Andrews, and Yale-NUS College.

Amelia Bonea is an historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2004) and Heidelberg University (~2006–2012). Circa 2020, she became Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester.

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate from the University of Oxford in 2012 and held posts at Naropa University and Central Michigan University (both attested 2019).

Amin Sweeney was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of London (~1967–1970). He taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and UC Berkeley (1986–1991), becoming emeritus professor in 1998.
Amita Chatterjee is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage was an Indologist and linguist. He was Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College (~1961–1978) and Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993–2003).
